testcase.name: the original adjacent-pair merge still works
a night with one short interruption is detected as a single session
two consecutive active runs are not absorbed
the same night with a genuinely awake interruption is not bridged into one
an active run past the default bound is absorbed when HR stays in the sleep band
a short interruption with elevated HR is not absorbed
an active run longer than the bound is left alone
the wider bound does not apply when HR is elevated
a blocked pair reports the bound that blocked it, with the active length
the in-band bound is a maximum, never a replacement
the pair line renders exactly as its Swift twin does
a brief spike no longer puts the whole interval out of band, a sustained one still does
an adjacent-pair merge reports no active bound
a short active interruption between two sleep runs is absorbed
the traced pass returns exactly what the plain one does
